case_0412.title: State v. Ravi Kumar
case_0412.full_text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF DELHI AT NEW DELHI
CRL.A. 1274/2019

STATE OF NCT OF DELHI ... Appellant
VERSUS
RAVI KUMAR ... Respondent

Date of Judgment: 18.09.2019

1. This appeal arises from an order of the learned Sessions Court granting bail to the respondent, who stands accused of an offence under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The prosecution's case is that the respondent, along with two co-accused, was involved in an altercation that resulted in the death of the complainant's brother on the night of 3 February 2019. The respondent was arrested on 6 February 2019 and has remained in judicial custody since.

3. Learned counsel for the State submits that the gravity of the offence, coupled with the respondent's alleged role as the primary assailant, warrants the cancellation of bail. It is further submitted that there exists a reasonable apprehension of the respondent influencing witnesses, several of whom reside in the same locality.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent submits that the respondent has no prior criminal record, has permanent roots in the community, and has fully cooperated with the investigation, including furnishing all requisitioned documents and appearing before the investigating officer on each occasion required.

5. Having considered the material on record, including the status report filed by the investigating agency, this Court finds that the custody period of over 90 days, taken together with the respondent's clean antecedents and cooperative conduct, weighs in favour of maintaining the bail order.

6. Accordingly, the accused shall be released on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000 with one surety of the like amount, subject to the conditions that the respondent shall not leave the jurisdiction of this Court without prior permission and shall appear before the trial court on every date of hearing.

7. The appeal is dismissed. The interim order, if any, stands vacated.
summary_sentences: The appeal challenges a Sessions Court order granting bail under Sections 302 and 34 IPC.
The respondent was arrested on 6 February 2019 and has remained in custody since.
The respondent has no prior criminal record and has cooperated fully with the investigation.
The custody period of over 90 days weighs in favour of maintaining the bail order.
The accused shall be released on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000 with one surety.

case_0198.title: Suresh Nair v. State of Kerala
case_0198.full_text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM
B.A. No. 3021 of 2021

SURESH NAIR ... Petitioner
VERSUS
STATE OF KERALA ... Respondent

Date of Order: 11.06.2021

1. This is an application for bail filed by the petitioner, who is accused of offences under Sections 420, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code in connection with an alleged forgery of property documents.

2. The petitioner has been in judicial custody for 94 days. The prosecution submits that the investigation is at an advanced stage, with the majority of documentary evidence already seized and forwarded for forensic examination.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the offence is compoundable in nature, that the petitioner has no other criminal antecedents, and that further custody serves no investigative purpose given that the material evidence has already been secured.

4. This Court finds that a custody duration of 94 days, in an offence of this nature and where the documentary evidence is already in the custody of the investigating agency, is disproportionate to any continuing investigative need.

5. The petitioner is granted bail subject to executing a bond of Rs. 50,000 with two sureties of the like amount each, and on the condition that the petitioner shall not tamper with evidence or contact prosecution witnesses.

6. The bail application is allowed accordingly.
summary_sentences: The petitioner seeks bail on charges of forgery under Sections 420, 468 and 471 IPC.
The petitioner has been in custody for 94 days while the investigation nears completion.
Documentary evidence has already been seized, reducing the need for further custody.
The custody duration is found disproportionate given the state of the investigation.
Bail is granted on a bond of Rs. 50,000 with two sureties.
